_comment: FAST PC News - the LATEST items on About -> PC News
Written nightly by the news sweep step of the daily-intel-watch scheduled task, committed
here on main, and published to fast-updates/intel/ by tools/Publish-IntelFeed.ps1, which
refuses the file if any rule below is broken. FAST also ships this copy and uses whichever
is newer (PcNewsData.Load). PcNewsFileTests pins the same rules on the shipped copy.
THE PAGE IS FREE AND ONLY INFORMS. An item says what happened, who it affects and where it
came from. Whether to install or roll back a driver, and what to do about a Windows update,
is the advice on the paid GPU Drivers and System Score pages, so no item gives it.
FIELDS (every item):
id       - stable, unique, lower-case words and hyphens, e.g. 2026-10-21-nvidia-621-01-black-screens
date     - yyyy-MM-dd the news happened (not the day the sweep found it)
kind     - problem | release
category - problems only: stability (crashes, black screens, freezes, games that will not
start) | performance (FPS, stutter, latency) | security
status   - problems only: confirmed (the vendor, Microsoft or Epic says so) | reported
(at least two independent outlets or threads, no vendor statement yet)
headline - up to 100 characters, FAST's own words
summary  - up to 400 characters, one or two sentences, FAST's own words, consequence first
applies  - tags FAST matches against this PC in code, OR'd: all | gpu:nvidia | gpu:amd |
gpu:intel | gpu-name:<text in the GPU name, e.g. RTX 50> | cpu:intel | cpu:amd |
cpu-name:<text in the CPU name, e.g. i9-14> | game:fortnite | app:obs
sources  - [{ name, url }], https only; a reported problem needs two
expires  - yyyy-MM-dd, no more than 31 days after date
SECURITY ITEMS ALSO HAVE:
audience - who is affected, in plain words; say so when ordinary gaming PCs are not
action   - optional, what to do (update the browser, rotate keys). Security only.
RULES: no advice in headline or summary; no em dashes; never name a product as the cause of
someone's problem unless its maker said so; never claim anything works with an anti-cheat;
a single article or a rumour is not news; at most 12 live items.

items.headline: Capcom confirms a breach of CAPCOM ID that exposed about 11.7 million account emails
items.summary: Capcom says attackers got into CAPCOM ID, the account system behind its websites and some online games, and took email addresses and sign-in details such as the last login time and IP address for about 11.7 million accounts. Capcom says card details were not involved and it has found no sign that passwords were taken; it reset 196 accounts whose passwords the attackers changed.
items.audience: Anyone with a CAPCOM ID account. The PC itself is not affected.
items.action: Be wary of emails or messages about your Capcom account, and do not open their links or attachments. Turning on two-factor sign-in where you can is a sensible precaution.

items.headline: Critical PHP flaws nicknamed PHP2Shell are being targeted on web servers
items.summary: PHP released fixes on October 21 for two critical flaws that let attackers run code on web servers running PHP, and security firms report widespread scanning and exploit attempts. The flaws are in server software, not in Windows or games.
items.audience: Website owners and hosting providers running PHP on their servers. Ordinary gaming PCs are not affected.
items.action: Nothing to do on a gaming PC.

items.headline: October's Windows security update fixes a flaw attackers were already using
items.summary: Microsoft's October 13 security update fixes CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that attackers were exploiting to slip past the warning Windows shows on files downloaded from the internet. It needs someone to open a booby-trapped file or link, and the same update fixes two other flaws that were public before the patch.
items.audience: Every Windows PC that has not yet installed the October 13, 2026 security update or a later one.
items.action: Keep Windows updated: open Windows Update and install the latest security update if it is waiting.

items.headline: NVIDIA fixes high-severity security flaws in its GeForce drivers
items.summary: NVIDIA's September security bulletin lists flaws in its GPU display driver that could let a program already running on a PC gain higher privileges or run code in the kernel. On Windows, GeForce drivers older than 616.56, 610.88 and 582.78, depending on the driver branch, are affected.
items.audience: PCs with an NVIDIA graphics card on a GeForce driver older than 616.56, 610.88 or 582.78, depending on the branch. An attacker must already be able to run a program on the PC.
